independence.auction: For rational discriminant d, compute floor(sqrt(floor(d*10^120))) with integer isqrt, producing rational endpoints l,u with l^2<=d<=u^2. Substitute these into 2z/(p0+sqrt(d)) with reversed endpoint order. Check inventory membership, endpoint revenue inequalities and interval width. Exact square discriminants, zero target, constant price, capacity equality and insufficient capacity have separate branches. This uses neither Decimal sqrt nor the author checker's 160-step bisection. Midpoint error is below 10^-54 sale units in the checked interior cases; rounded model sale must lie within the rational enclosure expanded by 10^-39.
independence.dated_cash: A wallet ledger starts with separate Alder, Beacon, public and buyer cash endowments and zero recipient pockets. Every payment debits funded cash and credits the actual recipient. Run funders are individual creditors, not a single residual deficit; each waiting or unpaid principal claim survives to the appropriate late waterfall. Terminal asset cash is added once across retained and sold units. Recipient sums and institution-level loss allocations are then derived from those transfers.
independence.game: Enumerate individual unilateral deviations across WW, RR, RW and WR using the independent payoff wallets; WR follows by the explicit symmetry of the two original funder contracts. Compute the affine indifference zero only when opposite payoff-gap signs are resolved outside the stated numerical band. Cases with zero premium and complete indifference exercise the distinction between strict equilibria, weak numerical candidates and null mixed output.
independence.comparison_scope: Compare every field of each cutoff ledger, terminal recovery, Beacon allocation, funded buyer/public balance, resolution result and game output in the chosen cases. Financial strings are checked as finite decimal syntax then rational values within 10^-34 relative-to-max(1,abs(expected)) tolerance. Counted comparisons include serialization, structure, hashes and repeated printed-value ledgers; they are not a count of independent theorems or distinct economic cases.

proof_audit.topic: Auction existence, uniqueness and smallest sufficient sale
proof_audit.reason: On [0,S] subset [0,N], p0>0 and 2*lambda*N<=p0 imply continuous strictly increasing R(s)=p0*s-lambda*s^2 whenever S>0. A derivative of zero at the final point does not create a flat interval; integrating the derivative over any positive-length subinterval is positive. For S=0 the only feasible sale and target are both zero. Continuity and R(0)=0 give a unique sufficient sale exactly for 0<=z<=R(S). The rationalized smaller quadratic root equals the usual smaller root; lambda=0 gives z/p0. Equality at capacity is feasible; beyond capacity selling all free inventory is the maximum feasible funding action on this domain. Uniform-price proceeds are s*p(s), not the integral of the price schedule.

Independent deviation wallets give d0=-3.1 and d1=26-10sqrt(2)>0 for run minus wait. This proves exactly WW/RR pure equilibria. The affine gap has one interior zero, so both mixing players must use the same probability; a player facing a pure opponent has a strict best response, excluding one-mixer equilibria. None of this selects among equilibria or calibrates a crisis probability. At complete-indifference inputs all four profiles are weak candidates and no strict profile is returned; null mixed output is correctly not treated as a theorem denying a continuum of mixtures.

A=20+100q and E=100q-80 give d(A/E)/dq=(100E-100A)/E^2=-10000/E^2 for E>0. Retiring principal at the same mark preserves equity; borrowing cash with an equal liability also preserves it. At q=.9 prepayment A/E=110/10, then principal retirement38 gives72/10. Fundamental retained payoff80 minus remaining principal62 gives18 before the6.2 wait premium; terminal shareholder cash is11.8. These do not equal principal marked equity10. E=0 atq=.8, sale40 and revenue32. The lab gives no finite positive leverage ratio for nonpositive principal marked equity.

proof_audit.topic: Collateral, senior recourse and distinct funding
proof_audit.reason: The line draw is bounded jointly by cash deficit, committed cap and advance*p0*N. Reserved draw/(advance*p0) units are not saleable. The initial public cash80 and buyer cashp0*N=100 are separate actual endowments, each debited on transfer. The public claim is explicitly senior on Alder's entire retained estate, not a nonrecourse recovery capped at pledged units. The lower-advance intervention reserves all100 units against a50 loan, leaves an early private cash gap, and later repays the senior loan and private arrears from the retained estate. No pledged inventory or public cash is used twice.

proof_audit.topic: Two-cutoff payment priority and credit transmission
proof_audit.reason: Early retail, requested funder payments and Beacon consume only current Alder cash. Surviving runner principal, waiting promises and network arrears share the late private residual after public repayment. Beacon's early customer uses only its own usable cash, early network receipts and a timely bridge; a later receipt can pay arrears but cannot erase a recorded missed deadline. The own-cash, partial-bridge and no-bridge interventions verify those distinct mechanisms.

Summing the actual Alder transfers yields E0-H+private_claim_loss+public_loss=N(p0-v)+waiting_interest+buyer_gain. Independently, Beacon's network impairment equals its lost opening equity plus residual customer loss plus bridge loss. The network impairment is not added again after allocation to these bearers. Across the whole ledger, retail, individual funders, customer, both shareholders, public cash and buyer wealth equal all four original cash endowments plusvN. The network receipt cancels internally. Sale gains are transfers; the model has no real output destruction or tax cost from which to derive a general welfare loss.

Cap80 additionally funds all stated cutoff1 claims in every profile with draws18/49/80, so it provides stronger off-equilibrium payment coverage without being proved minimal or optimal. Holding cap80/RR cash history fixed, v.6 makes the public80 claim recover60 and lose20; the public vehicle ends with60. Replacing the known benchmark payoff with.6 instead changes best replies: the bounded peer intervention makes RR the strict equilibrium for all three tested caps. The stated timely stay, pari-passu restructured principal, cancellation of the6.2 aggregate WW premium and public priority over Beacon are original assumed rights. The stay neither creates usable cash nor increasesvN. The bridge comes from the stated public endowment; its deep-downside loss follows from the debtor's actual estate. The comparison honestly separates changed private rights, cash timing, principal losses and unsupported implementation/current-law claims.

financial_interventions.name: flat_price
financial_interventions.purpose: Remove price impact while holding contracts and asset value fixed; waiting becomes strictly dominant without support.

financial_interventions.name: all_actions_indifferent
financial_interventions.purpose: Flat price plus multiplier1 makes all actions payoff-indifferent; verify strict/weak/mixed-limit distinctions.

financial_interventions.name: zero_wait_premium
financial_interventions.purpose: Retain nonlinear liquidation but remove the premium; RR remains strict while WW is only a near-band weak candidate.

financial_interventions.name: known_downside_changes_game
financial_interventions.purpose: Set the known benchmark and terminal payoff to.6 across all three caps; recalculate action incentives instead of treating the downside only as a frozen-history stress.

financial_interventions.name: lower_advance
financial_interventions.purpose: At advance.5 and cap80, reserve all assets against only50 cash; test early private arrears, no double sale, full senior-estate recourse and later recovery.

financial_interventions.name: funded_A_equity
financial_interventions.purpose: Increase opening Alder cash and matching equity by10; rebuild liquidation needs from an actually funded balance sheet.

financial_interventions.name: Beacon_own_cash
financial_interventions.purpose: Increase Beacon cash and equity by5 under cap20; change its deadline resilience without changing the upstream debt or receipts.

financial_interventions.name: partial_bridge
financial_interventions.purpose: Bridge only3 against customer10; separate early missed7 from full later recovery.

financial_interventions.name: no_bridge
financial_interventions.purpose: A stay with no new cash leaves the full early miss despite a sound later estate.

financial_interventions.name: zero_public_budget
financial_interventions.purpose: Remove public cash, line cap and bridge consistently; no support can be created by promise alone.

financial_interventions.name: zero_terminal_assets
financial_interventions.purpose: Apply a zero-payoff state to fixed cap20/cap80 histories; test public/customer losses and wealth conservation at a zero estate.

financial_interventions.name: exact_sale_capacity
financial_interventions.purpose: Reduce each funder principal to16 and increase matching opening equity to50; RR target50 exactly reaches full-inventory revenue, distinct from a funding failure.

financial_interventions.name: funded_no_sale
financial_interventions.purpose: Opening cash38 and matching equity38 cover the no-run early payments; exercise a true zero-sale branch with conserved resources.
